message.content:
Below are two practical ways to capture a screenshot of whatever is currently displayed in Google Chrome:

| Goal | Recommended approach | Why it works |
|------|----------------------|--------------|
| **Open a URL yourself and grab a screenshot** | Selenium + ChromeDriver | Selenium controls a fresh Chrome instance; you can set viewport size, scroll, etc. |
| **Grab the *already‑open* Chrome window** | OS‑level screenshot (pyautogui + pygetwindow) or Chrome DevTools Protocol (pychrome) | These let you capture the exact pixels that Chrome is rendering, even if you didn’t start it yourself. |

---

## 1️⃣  Selenium – “Open a URL and screenshot”

### 1.1  Install the dependencies

```bash
pip install selenium webdriver-manager pillow
```

`webdriver-manager` automatically downloads the matching ChromeDriver binary, so you don’t have to manage it manually.

### 1.2  Basic script

```python
from selenium import webdriver
from webdriver_manager.chrome import ChromeDriverManager
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options
import time

# Optional: run Chrome headless (no UI)
options = Options()
options.add_argument("--headless")          # comment out if you want to see the browser
options.add_argument("--disable-gpu")
options.add_argument("--window-size=1920,1080")  # set viewport size

# Create the driver
service = Service(ChromeDriverManager().install())
driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=service, options=options)

try:
    url = "https://www.example.com"
    driver.get(url)

    # Wait for the page to load fully (you can replace this with explicit waits)
    time.sleep(3)

    # Grab a screenshot – either as a PNG file or as a base64 string
    driver.save_screenshot("screenshot.png")          # writes to disk
    # base64_str = driver.get_screenshot_as_base64()   # returns a base64 string

finally:
    driver.quit()
```

> **Tip:**  
> *If you want to capture the *entire* page (including off‑screen parts), use Selenium’s `execute_cdp_cmd` to call Chrome DevTools directly:*

```python
full_page = driver.execute_cdp_cmd(
    "Page.captureScreenshot",
    {"format": "png", "fromSurface": True}
)
with open("full_page.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(base64.b64decode(full_page["data"]))
```

---

## 2️⃣  Capture an *existing* Chrome window

Sometimes you already have Chrome running (maybe opened by a user) and you just want to grab what’s on the screen. Two common ways:

### 2.1  OS‑level screenshot (works on Windows, macOS, Linux)

#### 2.1.1  Install the helpers

```bash
pip install pyautogui pygetwindow pillow
```

#### 2.1.2  Script

```python
import pyautogui
import pygetwindow as gw
import time

# Find the Chrome window (by title or class)
chrome_windows = [w for w in gw.getAllWindows() if "Chrome" in w.title]
if not chrome_windows:
    raise RuntimeError("No Chrome window found")

# Pick the first one (or iterate over all)
win = chrome_windows[0]

# Bring it to the front (optional but useful)
win.activate()
time.sleep(0.5)  # give it a moment to come to the front

# Get window geometry
x, y, width, height = win.left, win.top, win.width, win.height

# Grab the region
screenshot = pyautogui.screenshot(region=(x, y, width, height))
screenshot.save("chrome_window.png")
```

> **Note:**  
> *On macOS you may need to grant “Screen Recording” permissions to the terminal or IDE that runs the script.*

### 2.2  Chrome DevTools Protocol (pychrome)

If Chrome was started with the `--remote-debugging-port=9222` flag, you can connect to it and ask Chrome to capture its own screenshot.

#### 2.2.1  Install pychrome

```bash
pip install pychrome
```

#### 2.2.2  Script

```python
import pychrome
import base64

# Connect to the debugging endpoint
browser = pychrome.Browser(url="http://127.0.0.1:9222")

# Grab the first tab (or filter by URL)
tab = browser.list_tab()[0]
tab.start()

# Capture screenshot
result = tab.call_method("Page.captureScreenshot", format="png")
image_bytes = base64.b64decode(result["data"])

with open("devtools_screenshot.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(image_bytes)

tab.stop()
```

> **How to enable remote debugging:**  
> *Launch Chrome from the command line:*  
> ```bash
> # Windows
> start chrome.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222
> 
> # macOS / Linux
> /Applications/Google\ Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google\ Chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222
> ```

---

## 🎯 Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Have Chrome installed (any recent version). |
| ✅ | For Selenium: `webdriver-manager` will fetch the right ChromeDriver. |
| ✅ | For OS‑level: `pyautogui` + `pygetwindow` + `pillow`. |
| ✅ | For DevTools: launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`. |
| ✅ | Run the script from a terminal that has permission to read the screen (macOS: Screen Recording). |

---

| pychrome | https://github.com/fate0/pychrome |
